An index of the findings in this repository's records, one line each, for looking up before a run is declared, a cost is priced or two
constructions are compared. It exists because a session's memory of the work is a summary of a summary, and a link was lost that way:
on November 10, 2026 the speed review recorded that a 12288-wide solve ran out of memory on a 16 GB card and how the solver of that day
got past it one path at a time; on November 13 a 12288-wide solve was launched on that card, ran out of memory again, and a card was
rented for it (Marcos, November 13: "YALL ARE MISSING THE LINKS ON THE RESEARCH BECAUSE OF OCMPATION").

How to use it. Search it for the subject before acting on it: the matrix or width (`12288`, `ffn_down`), the card, the run's name, the
instrument, the quantity. `grep -n -i '12288' records/KNOWN.md`. Each line is
`KIND | subject keys | the finding, in the record's own numbers | path:line`. The record at path:line holds, not this line: open it
before a decision rests on it. This page is never read whole and is not loaded into a session; `STATE.md` names it.

The kinds: LIMIT, a wall that was hit (card memory, time, precision, disk, a difference between the two cards). PAST, a way that got
past a limit, or a saving, and whether it was adopted. FAILED, what did not work, with the reason the record gives. HELD, what was
measured or shown, with its numbers. TRAP, a mistake of method or reading that was made and corrected. OPEN, what a record says is
unresolved, untried or not built. CORRECTED, a statement a later line of the same record corrects.

How it was made, and what that is worth. On November 13, 2026, six readers with no memory of the work each read a slice of the records line by line
(73 files, listed below as the headings) and returned these 1964 lines (959 HELD, 302 TRAP, 234 LIMIT, 228 FAILED, 165 OPEN, 65 PAST, 11 CORRECTED).
Every cited file exists. Each line's numbers were then looked for at the lines it cites, three lines either side: 1037 lines have
every number there, 48 have some and 49 none (both marked at the end of the line), and 830 state no number.
The wording of a finding is a reader's and was not checked: a line here is a pointer, never a source. Records not read: the runs'
own `result.json` and `declaration.json` files, the tools' READMEs, and anything written after it was made.

How it is kept. A record that states a limit, a way past one, a failure or a finding adds its lines here, under its own heading, in
the commit that adds the record. A line found wrong is fixed or removed, with the record. When a section has drifted from its record,
the section is read again from the record and replaced.

## Trainer host memory, working files and remote test runs, November 19

- The joint trainer's host memory was never the model (11.5 GB on card 0): it was four whole FP32 arrays of the trainable weights (leaves 7.51 GB, remainder 7.51 GB, direction 7.78 GB, displacement 7.78 GB), one 3.96 GB native trace per member at 2,048 events, and each member's whole gradient, all alive together; the continuation's unit held 57 GB of RAM and 9 GB of shared memory. [Cause and build](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md)
- The streamed build keeps those four arrays in files whose pages are returned after every phase (`host_pages.Store`), sums each leaf's gradient into the direction file as it arrives, and reads a fresh native trace from its capture's stream one merge at a time; what the host still holds whole is what the measurement forms from one member's trace, about 2.6 GB float64 plus 1.3 GB float32 at the event cap. [Limits](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#what-is-not-bounded-by-this-build)
- The working files are 39,895,039,168 bytes at their largest and the launcher's `check` asks for 118,965,425,616 bytes free; the cohort capture reserve is counted twice (22.03 GB against about 5 GB a cohort has taken). [Disk cost](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#what-it-costs-in-disk)
- `final_experiment.prepare` refuses any build in which one of the nine lineage-bound sources of `vector-chance-final-experiment-installed-348-recovery` changed; the reviewed way through is an open revision of a prior declaration that names every changed source and binds an independent review, and the better fix is a launcher that accepts an explicit reviewed source revision. [Route and gate](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#the-lineage-guard-and-how-the-run-is-declared)
- A name that an observability inventory hooks cannot be removed from its module without both inventories (`pipeline/observability/instrumentation.py` and the frozen `capture.py`): commit 800cfd81 removed `vector_chance.turns` and the next start recorded `ops.instrumentation_setup_error` for `computation.turns`. [The hook](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#the-hook-that-had-lost-its-target)
- A plotting backend that opens the display ties a headless trainer's life to the X server: the continuation died on an X IO error at 10:50:39 PM CT November 18; the launcher now removes `DISPLAY`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and `XAUTHORITY` and sets `MPLBACKEND=Agg`. [Cause and build](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md)
- A release that removes a file's other hard-linked names breaks every declaration that names one of them: `vector-chance-full-weight-training/final-remainder.f32` left with its twin on November 19, twelve finished declarations read as drift, and the file came back by `archive_inputs.py restore 4c706e190fdb-remainder.f32.json --fetch` and `ln`. What went wrong
- The archive tool cannot take a derived array whose provenance does not state the SHA-256 of the original it was made from, nor a file no record of its run hashes: 97 such files, 41.22 GB, stayed local on November 19. What stayed
- Unit suites run in Linux on the secondary test host with `remote-runner exec --to runner@test-host -- sh -c 'docker run … uv run … python -m unittest <modules>'`; the remote runner ships the tree without the sealed directory (96 tracked files it cannot read, never opened) and without the repository. [Where the tests ran](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#where-the-tests-ran)
- the remote runner's credential scan lets one `.gitleaksignore` fingerprint clear one finding on a line, so a one-line JSON record holding many hashes needs an allowlist in `.gitleaks.toml` (rule, path and 64-hex secret, all three), which the project's lead or the President decides; the 4,707 false positives of November 19 are array names, token-list hashes, measured numbers and two file hashes, each held to its kind by `checked.py`. Checked findings · Config
- A declared parameter's `measured_from` is one record path: a list there crashes `verify_round2.py:97` for every seat, so a number read from several records cites the first and names the others in its derivation (`group_contrast_experiment.declare_disk`; `records/development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md`).
- A resumed run is held to a recorded one by `records/development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/gate.py <resumed> <recorded> --through N --watch <unit>`: every record the recorded run holds is required, values are compared exactly, and the trainer's unit gets SIGTERM at the first difference.
- The pipeline's unit tests run off this machine with `tools/remote-tests.sh [modules]`: Linux in Docker on the secondary test host, the trainer's own versions; with no argument it discovers every module under `code/signal-trace/tests`. Run at 4:47 AM CT November 19 on the two streaming modules: 21 tests, OK. `tools/remote-tests.sh`:1
- A declaration made outside `final_experiment.prepare` must add its own run to `consumed_trace_archive.active_runs`: the frozen loop archives a consumed observation only for a run that list names, and the first streamed start stopped itself there after update 1 (5:39 AM CT November 19, `ValueError: the current run must remain in the archive active-input guard`); the launcher's `check`, the unit tests and the review do not exercise that step. [Why it stopped](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#what-the-first-streamed-start-measured)
- The streamed trainer's unit peaked at 15.6 GB by systemd's count against 63.4 GB before, not the few GB predicted: anonymous memory 7.5 to 7.7 GB through a proposal and 11.35 GB at most in a measurement, plus a whole working store resident (8.4 to 8.6 GB of mapped file pages) during the restore, the install and the receipts. [Measured table](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#what-the-first-streamed-start-measured) · samples
- `posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)` drops neither mapped nor dirty pages, so a thread that sweeps a file's cache (`host_pages.Dropper`) does nothing for a `Store` while a pass maps it: only `Store.release()` (flush, `madvise(DONTNEED)`, then the advise) returns those pages, and a pass that walks a whole store holds it whole until then. [What would bring the peak down](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#what-would-bring-the-peak-down-and-is-not-built)
- glibc raises its mapping threshold up to 32 MB as large blocks are freed, after which arrays under that size come from the heap and are not returned (5.08 GB of heap in the trainer at 5:22 AM CT November 19); `MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=131072` and `MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=131072` on the unit fix it at its initial value without touching a bound source, and each live array of 128 KiB or more then shows as its own anonymous mapping in `/proc/<pid>/smaps`. [The second streamed start](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#the-second-streamed-start)
- The joint trainer checks the disk before every acquisition, not once: it asks for 76,100,156,688 bytes free each time (next checkpoint 17.04 GB, cohort captures 11.02 GB, the machine's 40 GB, and 8.05 GB of working files still to be written), and the launcher's `check` at the start covers none of what other work takes later; the second streamed start stopped 51 MB under it at 7:13 AM CT November 19 after about 22.8 GB went to other use of the disk in 77 minutes. Whoever holds the run watches the free disk for its whole length. [Why it stopped](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#the-second-streamed-start)
- The two allocator variables did not bring the streamed trainer to a few GB: the proposal held the same 6.2 to 8.5 GB of anonymous memory, the unit's peak fell from 16.31 to 14.87 GB, and the run took 26 and 44 minutes for the baseline and the proposal against 16 and 29 on a machine whose load was 19 to 23; the third start does not set them. [Measured](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#the-second-streamed-start)
- The third streamed start passed the archive step after update 1 at 8:33:38 AM CT November 19 with all 22 compared records equal to the continuation's; its unit peaked at 17.49 GB (16.31 and 14.87 GB for the two before it, 63.4 GB for the continuation), free disk fell to 92.59 GB against the trainer's 76.10 GB, and the run's own folder reached 44.96 GB | records/development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md, "The third streamed start"
- Forcing released pages out of the page cache (`msync`, `MADV_DONTNEED`, then `POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED` on every release, with a thread dropping the model, checkpoint and capture files once a second) made the streamed trainer read every 7.5 to 9.3 GB file from the NVMe again in every phase: the third streamed start's unit read 2.38 TB and wrote 258 GB in four hours, 165 to 225 MB/s for the whole run with half the machine's memory free, and the machine lagged; a release now only takes the pages out of the process and the cache is the kernel's. [What the third start did to the disk](development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md#what-the-third-start-did-to-the-disk-and-the-change) | records/development/2026-11-19-streamed-working-state/README.md, "What the third start did to the disk, and the change"
- The joint trainer's frozen controller honors a stop only between updates (`run.py`, `while not stop`): a SIGTERM during an update is followed by the rest of that update, its measurement, the archive step and a 16.8 GB exit checkpoint, 53 minutes on the third streamed start (asked at 10:56:28 AM CT November 19, ended 11:49:37 AM CT), so nothing is loosened to hurry an exit.
